newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George, Advance trade halted.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George, Advance trade halted.

text.p: Regional banks St George Bank Ltd and Advance Bank Ltd said on Monday they had requested that trading in their shares on the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) be suspended pending the release of an announcement to the ASX.
A St George spokesman said he had no further comment on the announcement.
A spokesman for Advance Bank said a statement would be issued shortly but would not comment when asked if the announcement would deal with a mooted merger of the two Sydney-based banks.

"In view of the increase in the trading price of the company's securities traded over the last two days, the company believes it is in the best interests of the shareholders for further trading in the company's securities to be halted pending this announcement," Advance said in a statement.
It said the announcement, if any, would most likely be made on Monday morning and requested that the share halt expire at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) on Monday.
Advance Bank shares soared on Friday to a year's intra-day high of A$6.35 on speculation a merger was imminent, probably with St George. The stock ended 18 cents higher at A$6.28.
St George shares did not trade on Monday morning, and ended two cents higher at A$8.95 on Friday.

The two banks have been regarded as likely merger partners throughout calendar 1996 as the banking sector continued to rationalise. Advance chairman Jim Service said in July that a merger of the two banks had "obvious logic". Each bank was formerly a building society with most assets held in mortgages.
National Australia Bank Ltd took a 6.8 percent stake in St George earlier this year, with analysts speculating that a takeover bid was likely in the medium term.
